title: Titanium Dental Abutment
alloyReason: ASTM F136 Ti-6Al-4V ELI is specified for Titanium Dental Abutment as an implant-grade material where controlled interstitial chemistry delivers consistent fatigue strength (>600 MPa @ 10^7 cycles) and crevice corrosion resistance for permanent implantation. The restricted aluminum (5.5-6.5%) and vanadium (3.5-4.5%) ranges ensure reproducible mechanical performance for Modular dental abutment retaining screw. This rationale is driven by modular dental abutment retaining screw and fat life requirements.
process: CNC swiss turning for dental geometry
Ultrasonic clean Class 10k for net-shape tolerance
surfaceTreatment: Electropolishing + passivation per ASTM F86 (20-30% HNO3, 30min @50C) achieving Ra <0.2um for implant-grade finish — tailored for modular dental abutment application
commonFailures: Fatigue fracture at thread root under cyclic bending - resolved by thread rolling (not cutting) for compressive stress — critical for modular dental abutment performance

Process traceability covers all manufacturing steps with batch records, inspection results, and device history records — compliant with FDA 21 CFR Part 820 and ISO 13485 requirements.
